ANOTHER  Appearance:
 Applicant by Shri Ritu Raj Bhatnagar - Advocate.
Respondent - State of Madhya Pradesh by Shri Kamal Ku  Government Advocate appearing on behalf of Advocate General.

ORDER This repeat (second) application under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (equivalent to Section 439 of Cr.P.C.) for grant of regular bail has been filed by applicant - Rama @
Ramlal S/o Goba Bhabhar Bhil, who has been arrested on 03.06.2024 in connection with Crime No.185 of 2024 registered at Police Station Nahargarh, District Mandsaur (M.P.) for commission of offence under Sections 363, 366-A, 376 (2) (N), 342 and 506 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 and also under Sections 3 / 4 and 5 / 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
First application of the applicant was dismissed by this Court as withdrawn vide order dated 17.01.2025 passed in Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.43482 of 2024 with a liberty to renew the prayer after examination NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9426 2 MCRC-12800-2025 of the prosecutrix and her parents before the trial Court.
2.
As per prosecution case, the allegation against the applicant is that he has committed rape on minor prosecutrix.
Accordingly, a case has been registered against him.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that as per the prosecution case, the incident took place on 22.05.2024 and the applicant has been apprehended on 03.06.2024 and suffering incarceration of near about ten months.
Age of the victim has been alleged told as fourteen years and four months.
The applicant is also of nineteen years of age.

The prosecutrix and other material prosecution witnesses including her father have been examined before the trial Court and they have not supported the prosecution case, but there are material embellishment in the statement of the Rama @ Ramlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197469598/
1 prosecutrix.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Trial will take time, as victim along with material prosecution witnesses have been examined and there are no chances of tampering with the evidence, therefore, learned counsel prays for allowing the bail application and for grant of bail.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State has vehemently opposed the prayer as victim is below sixteen years of age and has supported the prosecution case; and prays for dismissal of the bail application.
5.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

6. In the aforesaid factual backdrop, looking to the evidence in entirety and the statement of the prosecutrix and her father and maternal uncle, this Court is inclined to grant benefit of bail to the applicant.
Accordingly, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9426 3 MCRC-12800-2025 without commenting on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

7. It is directed that the applicant be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with separate solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by the said Court, without any default, during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480 (3) of BNSS.
8.
The applicant will not indulge himself in any criminal activity in future.

This order shall be effective till the end of the trial, however, in case of bail jump and / or breach of any of the conditions of bail, this order will come to an end and applicant will be liable to be arrested by the concerned authorities.
9. The concerned Court shall get the conditions reproduced on the personal bond by the accused and on surety bond by the surety concerned.
If any of them is unable to write, the scribe shall certify that he had explained the conditions to the concerned accused or the surety.
10. Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed off.
Certified copy as per rules.
(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE rcp Rama @ Ramlal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197469598/
